filename: One‐at‐a‐Time Parameter Perturbation Ensemble of the Community Land Model, Version 5.1
title: One‐at‐a‐Time Parameter Perturbation Ensemble of the Community Land Model, Version 5.1
venue: Journal of Advances in Modeling Earth Systems
code_availability: CTSM model code: https://github.com/ESCOMP/CTSM/tree/branch_tags/PPE.n11_ctsm5.1.dev030; ensemble generation scripts: https://github.com/djk2120/ppe_tools; analysis and figure generation code: https://github.com/djk2120/oaat_clm5_ppe
testbed_rationale: Provides a large, systematically varied perturbed parameter ensemble (over 2,000 simulations, 211 parameters perturbed across 6 climate forcing scenarios) with publicly accessible post-processed data on Dryad and model code on GitHub, suitable for land model emulation, parameter calibration, and sensitivity analysis.
pain_points: High computational cost of land biogeochemistry spin-up (managed using SASU matrix acceleration)
Spatial resolution cost trade-off (addressed via a 400-cluster sparse grid which introduces spatial interpolation errors that scale up for smaller domains)
Hard-coded model parameters in land models requiring manual refactoring into parameter files

Difficulty in establishing realistic parameter bounds with expert solicitation and ±20% heuristics, which caused plant functional type mortality for some extreme perturbations requiring manual constraints
One-at-a-time design cannot detect parameter interaction effects or nonlinearities
Prescribed data atmosphere omitting coupled land-atmosphere feedbacks that could modulate flux responses
extraction_notes: The primary ML method directly applied in the paper is multivariate spatio-temporal clustering (k-means) used to build the representativeness-based sparse grid. The dataset is explicitly designed to serve as a foundation for ML emulation, sensitivity quantification, and calibration.
